Business-logic DAST first, then application-layer attack surface management, then Cascade,
body_text: We've been approved for OpenAI's Trusted Access for Cyber preview. For years we've been building toward one idea: offensive security that runs continuously inside engineering, instead of arriving twice a year as a PDF nobody reads past the executive summary. Business-logic DAST first , then application-layer attack surface management, then Cascade, our AI pentesting agent. Three products on one offensive security engineering platform, because a list of assets, a stream of findings and a pentest report are only worth much together. Trusted Access for Cyber is the next piece. Our engineering and security teams now have verified access to OpenAI's models with less resistance on the dual-use security work that would normally trip a refusal. All of it goes toward one number: the time between a vulnerability existing and your team holding both a working exploit and the fix. That window is where an adversary does their work. Today it runs to months. It should be hours. Offensive security has become an AI workload. We've been building for that from the start, and TAC opens frontier models to the defenders doing the work and help turn insights into action faster. Reducing the time between discovery and remediation Attackers use AI for discovery. Endpoints, business logic flaws, and the chains that turn two small gaps into one real breach. That work starts to get parallelized cheaply and rewards volume. Defenders have mostly pointed AI at protection instead: threat modeling, alert triage, incident summaries, detection engineering. Meanwhile most scanners haven't kept up with frontier AI. So you get two clocks running at different speeds, and the distance between them is the number worth managing. Luckily, programs like OpenAI’s TAC give verified defenders a trusted route to apply frontier AI to cyber defense. Time to proof is the distance between a logic-level vulnerability existing in your application and your team holding a working exploit and a fix for it. Not a severity score. We want to provide actual proof an engineer can reproduce. For most organizations that distance runs to months, because it's set by the pentest calendar, the bug bounty queue, and whatever a scanner happens to cover, rather than by how long the vulnerability actually takes to find. In our published benchmark on two live open-source applications, Cascade set up in minutes and reported in hours, at a 0% false-positive rate across both blackbox and whitebox runs. On Photoview it went from 12 validated findings blackbox to 28 with the repository attached. Last week our research team disclosed a PII disclosure in Keycloak, now CVE-2026-17059 . The platform found it by asking every user-returning endpoint the same authorization question and comparing the answers, which is the kind of gap a code review reads straight past. Red Hat published the CVE six days after we reported it. Keycloak shipped the one-line fix four days later. Every finding came with a working exploit and remediation code attached. That's the part that matters, because a finding an engineer doesn't trust is a finding that doesn't get fixed, and an unfixed finding reduces nobody's exposure. What it changes for us The access is for our internal security research and engineering teams. What it improves is the research behind Cascade, and everything downstream that helps teams remediate exploitable vulnerabilities. Cascade is a harness: it decides how a set of agents explores an application, what it carries between steps, which hypothesis is worth chasing, and how a finding gets proven. Escape routes work across a portfolio of frontier AI models and open-weight models. No single provider or model powers the product end-to-end. We treat models as interchangeable components and select the best one for each sub-task based on continuous internal benchmarks. The harness is what we build, and with a stronger set of models underneath it reaches further. OpenAI makes the same observation in their announcement, that " sophisticated harnesses elicit stronger and stronger capabilities " with existing models. The two compound. Our mission hasn't changed. Five people should be able to defend a thousand-person engineering org. Escape velocity was never about going faster, it's the point where you stop falling back, and programs like this bring our mission closer to its goal. What this means for security teams A couple of things worth looking into: Annual pentest cadence is getting harder to defend. Pentesting was annual or quaterly because expert hours were scarce and required large budgets. AI changed those economics. If your attack surface changes weekly and your testing is yearly, the delta between those two numbers is your actual risk position. Our goal is to be helping customers manage risk as the threat landscape speeds up. That takes visibility you can trust across everything you expose, findings proven well enough that engineers act on them without arguing, and remediation that doesn't stall when the next critical vulnerability lands. Verified access is becoming part of vendor due diligence. Model providers are moving toward tiers based on proven identity and use case. Which frontier AI capabilities your security vendors can legitimately reach is now a fair question, alongside SOC 2 and data residency. Discovery has been compounding on the attacker's side for a while now. What programs like OpenAI’s Trusted Access for Cyber do is let it compound on the defender's side too, in the open. That's worth more than any single model release. Every verified defender who gets this kind of access makes the software all of us depend on a little harder to break. We're glad to be one of them, and what we find will keep going out in public.

title: Amentum to Support Critical Infrastructure and Platforms Under New Engineering Services Framework

body_text: Amentum to Support Critical Infrastructure and Platforms Under New Engineering Services Framework August 19, 2026 • Engineering & Design , Navy , Strategic Capabilities Engineering , UK Featured , Press Releases Share Image courtesy of Babcock International Group Award from Babcock enables support across nuclear, marine, land and aviation domains CHANTILLY, Va., August 19, 2026 – Amentum (NYSE: AMTM) has joined a five-year Babcock International Group Engineering Services Framework to support nuclear, marine, land, aviation and mission systems for the UK Armed Forces at home and abroad. The agreement forms part of a wider strategy to build closer, long-term partnerships with key suppliers, creating a simpler and more consistent way to bring specialist engineering expertise into critical defence programmes. The framework enables suppliers to support multiple projects more quickly, helping streamline procurement and strengthen collaboration. The award of the framework builds on decades of infrastructure support to Babcock’s Devonport Royal Dockyard, His Majesty’s Naval Base Clyde, and the Rosyth Royal dockyard, and enables on-going and future support to critical UK defence and submarine programmes, as well as broader support for platforms and infrastructure across the nuclear, marine, land, and air domains. “Our decades of naval nuclear infrastructure experience, the breadth and depth of our engineering and architectural skills, together with our unrivalled scientific reach back, makes Amentum a one-stop shop for Babcock’s engineering, nuclear and technical requirements,” said Loren Jones, senior vice president and head of Amentum’s Energy & Environment-International business. “We are looking forward to supporting the delivery of programmes vital to the UK’s safety and security in the years ahead, deploying our proven experience of modernizing the UK’s naval bases, dockyards and defence systems, including specialized technical validation for critical infrastructure such as docks, berths and shiplifts for the maintenance of Astute and Dreadnought-class submarines, and for the wider Royal Navy fleet.” Amentum provides complex programme, project and engineering solutions, including: requirements management; architectural design and building services; multi-disciplinary design engineering (marine, civil / structural, electrical, control and instrumentation and mechanical); and specialist technical support, such as safety case authoring, Human Factors, 3D Building Information Modelling, geotechnical studies, seismic / blast assessment and Independent Technical Assessment. Amentum also supports critical defence programmes more widely, providing research and technology services, safety case, and security services for the Royal Navy’s nuclear propulsion systems. Our commitments are underpinned by the belief that safety, collaboration and well-being are integral to success.Headquartered in Chantilly, Virginia, we have approximately 50,000 employees in more than 70 countries across all 7 continents. title: Cove Kaz Capital Group Advances Generational Tungsten Project
summary: Dominari Securities is dedicated to helping clients preserve, grow and create new wealth by providing a full range investment advisory and wealth planning services.
body_text: Announces Top Global Engineering Firms to Lead Definitive Feasibility Study (DFS) Northern Katpar DFS commences in July 2026 with anticipated completion before the end of 2027 NEW YORK & ASTANA, Kazakhstan--( BUSINESS WIRE )--Cove Kaz Capital Group LLC (“Cove Kaz Capital Group” or the “Company”), a U.S.-based company focused on the development of critical mineral resources in Kazakhstan, today announced it has engaged recognized global engineering firms to undertake a Definitive Feasibility Study (“DFS”) on the Northern Katpar tungsten project in Kazakhstan held by Severniy Katpar LLP, in which the Company holds a 70% controlling interest. The ultimate purpose of the DFS is to support a Final Investment Decision and facilitate the standard detailed due diligence requirements of prospective financing partners, including the U.S. International Development Finance Corporation (DFC), the Export-Import Bank of the United States (EXIM), other U.S. institutional finance entities, and commercial partners. The DFS will build into Front End Engineering and Design, which will then flow into detailed engineering and design, project construction, commissioning, and commercial operations. ﻿ Building on the Company’s technical leadership in the successful development and operation of large-scale tungsten assets, an extensive evaluation of the capabilities of leading engineering firms was performed. With that assessment, the Company determined a consortium of contractors is best qualified to meet the mining and refinery project’s objectives: DRA Global , an international multi-disciplinary engineering, project delivery and operations management group, predominantly focused on the mining, minerals and metals industry, has been appointed the lead contractor and will also be responsible for mineral processing; ERM , the world’s largest sustainability consultancy, providing comprehensive environmental, social, and risk advisory services for critical minerals projects, will lead on geology, mine planning, and technical programs, as well as environmental and social frameworks. ERM has extensive experience in major capital project environmental, social, regulatory, and financial license to operate and brings significant global and Kazakh mining experience to the project; and Knight Piésold , an international consulting firm providing specialized engineering and environmental services to the mining and energy sectors, with deep technical capability in tailings management, rock mechanics, and water management systems, supporting long-term operational safety and environmental resilience for complex large-scale tungsten mining operations, will lead on geotechnical, hydrology and tailings storage. These companies have been selected as preferred contractors subject to execution of definitive agreements and will work alongside Cove Kaz Capital Group’s highly experienced in-house team led by Chief Executive Officer Dominic Heaton. Mr. Heaton is widely recognized for having led the successful development of the Nui Phao integrated tungsten mine and refinery in Vietnam, the largest tungsten operation outside of China. The DFS will develop the overall mine plan for Northern Katpar and inform the construction and operations of its accompanying refinery to be located in Kazakhstan, designed to produce the benchmark tungsten product known as ammonium paratungstate (“APT”). “Following the start of site preparation in July, formally engaging the DFS engineering firms is an essential step towards our objective of becoming a leading, commercially successful supplier of tungsten to the United States,” said Pini Althaus, Executive Chairman, Cove Kaz Capital Group. “There is a systemic shortage of tungsten that cannot be addressed by existing mines globally, even in China. The current supply deficit is acute, but the medium to long-term market is also showing a significant shortage.” “We anticipate the DFS to be completed before the end of 2027 and it will be supported by extensive historical work by JSC Tau-Ken Samruk, the national mining company of Kazakhstan and our 30% partner in Severniy Katpar LLP,” said Mr. Heaton. “It is exciting to see the start of physical activity at the site after detailed planning since completing the acquisition of our controlling interest in Severniy Katpar in April. This was a months-long competitive evaluation process, and I would like to acknowledge the broad participation of best-in-class engineering firms seeking to support this project.” As the focus of activity at Northern Katpar transfers to the DFS, the Company is starting to ramp-up its development work on the second tungsten deposit held by Severniy Katpar LLP, known as Upper Kairakty, located approximately 25 kilometers from Northern Katpar. Severniy Katpar LLP owns one of the largest known undeveloped tungsten resources globally. Feasibility studies completed in April 2023 reported total JORC-compliant mineral resources containing 1.4 million tonnes of tungsten trioxide (WO3) and support anticipated production of approximately 5,000 metric tonnes per annum (mtpa) at Northern Katpar, and 7,000 mtpa from Upper Kairakty, for a total of 12,000 mtpa, representing approximately 15% of current global tungsten mine production. On April 29, 2026, Cove Kaz Capital Group acquired a 70 percent controlling interest in Severniy Katpar LLP, a joint venture with Kazakhstan’s national mining company Tau-Ken Samruk, which retains the remaining 30 percent. Through this partnership, Cove Kaz Capital Group will be developing the Northern Katpar and Upper Kairakty tungsten deposits, among the largest undeveloped tungsten resources globally. The project is advancing through feasibility, permitting, and development toward commercial production, with the objective of establishing a long-term, secure supply of tungsten to support critical industrial and high-technology applications in the United States and global markets. title: Penetration Rate Meaning: Definition & How to Calculate
summary: Discover the meaning of penetration rate and learn how to calculate it to boost your market strategy and customer conversion effectively.
body_text: Market penetration rate is the share of a defined target market that has purchased or used your product, expressed as a percentage. The formula is straightforward: (number of customers ÷ total target market) × 100 . Wall Street Prep documents this formula and stresses that estimating your total addressable market (TAM) before you calculate is the step most teams skip. The penetration rate meaning, in one sentence: it tells you how much of your available market you have actually converted into customers, not just reached or exposed to your brand. A dollar-based variant also exists: (total sales dollars ÷ total target market sales potential) × 100 . Both formulas answer the same question from different angles, and Investopedia explains when each is appropriate. One quick note on terminology: "penetration rate" appears in several fields, including mobile phone adoption and oil-drilling. When writing for marketing or product contexts, use "market penetration rate" to avoid ambiguity. Key Takeaways Market penetration rate is calculated as (customers ÷ total target market) × 100, and its accuracy depends entirely on how precisely you define the TAM and the customer counting rule before you run the numbers. Point Details Core formula (Customers ÷ TAM) × 100; a dollar-based variant uses total sales ÷ market sales potential × 100. Define TAM first Set eligibility criteria for your target market before calculating; population-level denominators distort results. Fix your time window Choose a consistent period (e.g., trailing 12 months) and hold it constant across all reporting cycles. Align counting rules Count unique buyers or active users, document the rule, and never mix definitions across periods. Pair with other metrics Combine penetration rate with churn, ARPU, and conversion rates for a complete strategic picture. Table of Contents What does penetration rate actually measure? How to calculate penetration rate step by step How to interpret your penetration rate results Common mistakes that distort your penetration rate Practical strategies to increase your penetration rate Industry examples and benchmark ranges An editorial perspective on using this metric well Sources What does penetration rate actually measure? Market penetration rate measures the proportion of a defined population that has taken a purchase or usage action, not just seen an ad or visited a page. Wikipedia defines it as the percentage of the relevant population that has purchased a brand or category at least once within the period under study. Common use cases include tracking a product launch, monitoring feature adoption inside a platform, validating whether a paid campaign drove actual conversions, and assessing how much runway remains in a given market. The metric is frequently confused with two others: Metric What it measures Unit Market penetration rate Share of target market that has purchased/used % of people or revenue Market share Your revenue as a share of total category revenue % of dollars Reach / awareness Share of population exposed to a message % of impressions SurveyMonkey notes the practical difference clearly: penetration counts behavioral conversion into customers, while market share counts revenue, and reach counts exposure. How to calculate penetration rate step by step Follow these four steps every time, and your results will be consistent and comparable across periods. Define your target population (TAM). Decide who could realistically buy your product. A B2B SaaS tool for mid-market finance teams in the U.S. has a very different TAM than "all businesses." Set a time window. Choose a fixed period, such as the trailing 12 months, and hold it constant across all calculations. Choose a customer counting rule. Decide whether you are counting unique purchasers, active subscribers, or lifetime buyers. Mixing these rules across periods invalidates comparisons. Apply the formula. Divide your customer count by the TAM and multiply by 100. Pro Tip: For subscription products, count only users active within your chosen time window, not all-time sign-ups. Lifetime counts inflate the rate and mask churn. Reporting both figures together is worth the extra step. High user penetration paired with low revenue penetration often signals a pricing or monetization gap, not a distribution problem. How to interpret your penetration rate results A high rate approaching the upper bound of your TAM suggests the market is maturing. Similarweb explains that penetration nearing saturation implies limited room for linear acquisition-driven growth, and that a strategic shift toward retention or product innovation becomes necessary. Context shapes everything here. Track the rate over time rather than reading a single snapshot. Cohort comparisons, such as comparing penetration among customers acquired in Q1 versus Q3, reveal whether your acquisition quality is improving. When penetration plateaus despite increased spend, that is usually the signal to shift focus: improve onboarding, reduce churn, or expand the product to serve adjacent segments rather than pushing harder on the same acquisition channels. Common mistakes that distort your penetration rate Getting the formula right is easy. Getting the inputs right is where most teams go wrong. Wrong denominator. Using total population instead of your actual TAM inflates the denominator and makes penetration look artificially low. Define TAM by realistic eligibility criteria, not census size. Inconsistent time windows. Comparing a 12-month count one quarter to a 6-month count the next produces a meaningless trend line. Double-counting customers. A customer who bought twice in the period is still one customer. Count unique buyers unless your metric is explicitly "transactions." Confusing reach with penetration. Ad dashboards sometimes label campaign reach as "penetration." Investopedia is explicit: penetration requires conversion into users or customers, not just exposure. Undocumented assumptions. If you change your TAM source or counting rule mid-year, every prior period becomes incomparable. Write your assumptions into a measurement spec and version-control it. Pro Tip: Before sharing a penetration figure with stakeholders, attach a one-line footnote: "TAM source: [X], customer definition: unique purchasers, time window: trailing 12 months." That single habit prevents most misinterpretations. Practical strategies to increase your penetration rate Moving the number requires deliberate choices across acquisition, retention, and product. Acquisition levers include targeted campaigns aimed at underserved segments within your TAM, channel expansion into distribution points your current customers don't use, and pricing experiments that lower the barrier to a first purchase. Knowing how to identify your target audience precisely is what separates a campaign that grows penetration from one that just recycles existing customers. Retention and usage levers matter more than most teams expect. Improving onboarding reduces early churn, which means each new customer actually stays in your "active" count. Product-led growth tactics, such as in-app prompts that drive cross-sell or usage milestones, increase the depth of adoption within your existing base. Measurement discipline ties it together. Run A/B tests or cohort-based analyses to isolate which lever actually moved the rate. Without a controlled comparison, you cannot tell whether a penetration gain came from a pricing change, a new channel, or seasonal demand. SaaS analytics approaches that tie campaign exposure to purchase events give you the clearest signal. Industry examples and benchmark ranges Penetration rates vary enormously by category, and any benchmark you find should be treated as directional, not prescriptive. The rate depends entirely on how TAM and customer rules are defined. Consumer packaged goods (CPG): Household penetration for a mainstream category brand can reach 30–60% of households in a given year, but niche brands often sit well below 5%. SaaS and B2B software: Enterprise tools targeting a narrow vertical commonly see single-digit penetration rates, even among well-known platforms. For context on how SaaS security products measure adoption, the eligible TAM is often a few thousand companies, not millions. Mobile apps: Consumer apps in large categories can achieve double-digit penetration of smartphone users, but retention, not initial install, determines whether that figure holds. Insurance: The NFIP residential penetration rate dataset from FEMA is one of the most disciplined public examples of penetration measurement: it computes insured residential structures as a ratio of total residential structures, with a clearly documented denominator and no ambiguity in counting rules. The FEMA example is worth studying regardless of your industry. The discipline of a fixed denominator definition and a transparent counting rule is exactly what makes a penetration metric trustworthy over time. An editorial perspective on using this metric well One thing we see consistently: teams spend more energy debating whether their penetration rate is "good" than they spend agreeing on what the denominator actually is. The metric is only as credible as the assumptions underneath it. Penetration rate works best as one lens among several. Pair it with churn rate to understand whether new customers are staying, with ARPU (average revenue per user) to catch monetization gaps, and with conversion rates at each funnel stage to identify where acquisition is breaking down. No single percentage tells the whole story, and presenting penetration in isolation to a leadership team often produces the wrong strategic conversation. Sources Market Penetration Rate | Formula + Calculator - Wall Street Prep Market penetration - Wikipedia Market penetration - Investopedia Market penetration: Calculation & A 6 Step Guide - Similarweb Market Penetration: What It Is, Strategies & How To Measure - SurveyMonkey Recommended How to Report Penetration Test Findings Effectively How to Do Pen Testing: A 2026 Professional Guide What Is Compliance Risk? 40% Fewer Violations Proven What Is Compliance Risk? 70% Cite Regulation Impact in 2026

title: How to Send a WhatsApp Blast: Complete Guide for Businesses in 2026
summary: Zoko is an all-in-one system that leverages the WhatsApp API to help you do business, on WhatsApp. Go beyond chatting - reach customers, enable product discovery, collect payments, get feedback - all on WhatsApp.
body_text: A WhatsApp blast can put a product launch, restock alert, limited-time offer, or important update directly into customers' conversations. The opportunity is especially strong in India. A 2025 Kantar study found that 91% of online adults in India chat with a business every week. WhatsApp also surpassed three billion users globally by June 2026. But sending more messages does not automatically create better marketing. Businesses need customer permission, relevant audience segments, suitable message templates, sensible frequency, and campaign tracking. This guide explains how to send a WhatsApp blast safely, which WhatsApp broadcasting option to use, and how e-commerce businesses can turn bulk messaging into targeted sales campaigns. ‍ What Is a WhatsApp Blast? A WhatsApp blast means sending the same core message to multiple customers at once. “WhatsApp blast” is an informal marketing term. WhatsApp itself provides several ways for businesses to send one-to-many messages, including standard broadcast lists, newer Business Broadcasts inside the WhatsApp Business app, and approved marketing templates through the WhatsApp Business Platform. Meta describes Business Broadcasts as a more advanced paid message type for businesses using the app. Businesses commonly use WhatsApp blasts for: Product launches Sales and promotions Back-in-stock alerts New collection announcements Seasonal campaigns Event reminders Customer re-engagement Reorder reminders Personalized product recommendations Unlike a WhatsApp Group, broadcast recipients receive messages privately. Their replies return as individual customer conversations. ‍ WhatsApp Blast vs. Broadcast vs. Group These terms are often mixed together, but they describe different communication methods. WhatsApp Messaging Methods Comparison Method How it works Best for WhatsApp blast Informal term for sending one campaign to many recipients Marketing and announcements Broadcast list Sends private messages to selected saved contacts Smaller contact lists Business Broadcast Paid broadcast feature inside the WhatsApp Business app Eligible small businesses Business Platform/API messaging Sends approved business messages at scale E-commerce and larger campaigns WhatsApp Group Members communicate inside one shared conversation Communities and discussions WhatsApp Channel One-way content distributed through the Updates tab Audience and content updates Businesses selling products usually need private broadcasts or API-based campaigns instead of groups. ‍ Three Ways Businesses Can Send a WhatsApp Blast ‍ The right method depends on audience size, automation needs, customer data, and campaign complexity. ‍ 1. Standard WhatsApp Broadcast Lists Classic broadcast lists work well for smaller audiences. WhatsApp currently allows up to 256 contacts in each broadcast list . WhatsApp also says contacts on the list need to have saved the sender's number in their address book. This method works for businesses with a relatively small customer base and simple campaigns. ‍ 2. Paid Business Broadcasts Meta has introduced Business Broadcasts inside the WhatsApp Business app. Unlike classic broadcast lists, Business Broadcasts are designed as a more advanced paid messaging option. Meta introduced the feature specifically to encourage businesses to be more deliberate about what they send. Availability and functionality can depend on the business account and current rollout. ‍ 3. WhatsApp Business Platform Businesses that need Shopify integration, customer segmentation, automation, larger campaigns, team workflows, and deeper tracking can use the WhatsApp Business Platform through Meta or a platform built on it. The Business Platform uses customer opt-in and approved templates for business-initiated messaging. For growing e-commerce stores, this approach makes it possible to connect WhatsApp campaigns with actual customer and purchase data. ‍ How to Send a WhatsApp Blast With a Standard Broadcast List ‍ For smaller audiences, the WhatsApp Business app provides the simplest starting point. ‍ Step 1: Build an Opted-In Contact List Collect phone numbers from customers who expect to hear from your business. Opt-in opportunities can appear during: Checkout Account creation Loyalty registration Website forms QR-code campaigns In-store purchases Product registrations Tell customers what type of WhatsApp communication they are signing up for. ‍ Step 2: Create a Broadcast List Create a new broadcast list inside WhatsApp Business and select the relevant contacts. Remember that standard lists currently support up to 256 contacts, and those contacts need to have saved your business number. ‍ Step 3: Write One Focused Message Keep each broadcast centered on one action. For example: The Summer Linen Collection is live. ‍ Lightweight styles designed for warmer days. Shop the collection: [link] Reply if you need help choosing your size. ‍ Step 4: Send and Manage Replies Recipients receive the broadcast privately and can reply directly to the business. This works for smaller campaigns. Larger stores usually need better segmentation, automation, scheduling, and conversion tracking. ‍ How to Send a WhatsApp Blast With the Business API The WhatsApp Business Platform provides a more scalable process for customer campaigns. ‍ Step 1: Connect Your Business to the WhatsApp Business Platform Businesses can access WhatsApp's business messaging infrastructure directly or through a provider. E-commerce businesses often connect it with systems such as: Shopify Customer profiles Product catalogs Order data Customer support tools Marketing automation This lets campaigns respond to actual customer behavior instead of operating from standalone phone-number lists. ‍ Step 2: Collect Clear WhatsApp Opt-Ins Businesses must obtain opt-in before sending message templates. Meta requires the opt-in to clearly communicate both the business name and the intent of the messages the customer will receive . For example: Receive product launches, restock alerts, and exclusive offers from Brand X on WhatsApp. Keep records showing how and when customers opted in. ‍ Step 3: Segment the Audience Do not send every WhatsApp blast to your entire customer database. Useful e-commerce segments include: First-time customers Repeat buyers VIP customers Customers interested in specific categories Customers from selected locations Recent purchasers Inactive customers Previous campaign responders Customers who have never ordered Segmentation makes the message more relevant to the person receiving it. ‍ Step 4: Create the Right Message Template WhatsApp templates are currently categorized as: Marketing: Promotions, offers, product recommendations, launches, and re-engagement Utility: Transactional communication connected to a customer action Authentication: Verification and authentication messages Meta requires each template to be categorized as marketing, utility, or authentication. A sale announcement belongs in a marketing template. Do not add promotional content to a utility message simply to avoid the marketing category. ‍ Step 5: Personalize the Message A broadcast does not need to read like a mass message. Personalization can use information such as: Customer name Previous purchase Product category Loyalty status Location Relevant collection Compare these two messages: Generic Big sale! Get 20% off today. Relevant Hey Maya, the skincare collection you purchased from last time is 20% off until midnight. The second message connects the offer to an existing customer relationship. ‍ Step 6: Test the Campaign Before sending, verify: Customer-name variables Product links Images Buttons Coupon codes Mobile formatting Landing pages Tracking links Audience exclusions Testing prevents a small configuration mistake from reaching thousands of customers. ‍ Step 7: Schedule and Send Choose timing based on customer geography, past engagement, campaign purpose, and purchase behavior. There is no universal send time that works equally well for every WhatsApp audience. ‍ Step 8: Prepare for Replies A successful broadcast can create a surge in customer questions. Prepare: Product information Quick replies Automated FAQ handling Sales agents Customer support routing AI chatbot support Clear human handover The broadcast earns attention. The conversation that follows can determine whether that attention becomes a sale. ‍ WhatsApp Blast Examples for E-commerce ‍ Product Launch Hi {{1}}, our new {{2}} collection just dropped. Explore the collection here: {{3}} ‍ Back-in-Stock Alert Good news, {{1}}. {{2}} is back in stock. View it here before your preferred option sells out: {{3}} ‍ Reorder Reminder Hi {{1}}, running low on {{2}}? Reorder your usual product here: {{3}} ‍ VIP Early Access {{1}}, you're getting first access. Our new collection opens tomorrow, but you can shop it today: {{2}} ‍ Win-Back Campaign It's been a while, {{1}}. We've added several new products since your last order. See what's new: {{2}} Each message should match the customer's consent and the actual purpose of the campaign. ‍ WhatsApp Blast Rules Businesses Need to Follow High-volume messaging requires more control than uploading a list and pressing send. ‍ Send Messages to Customers Who Opt In Meta requires businesses to obtain customer opt-in for message templates and clearly state the business and messaging purpose. Customers can also block businesses, report unwanted communication, and provide feedback about business messages. ‍ Respect WhatsApp's Marketing Message Limits WhatsApp can limit the number of marketing template messages an individual receives when that person is less likely to engage with them. There is no reason to chase maximum message volume. Sending fewer campaigns to better-matched audiences can produce a healthier customer experience. ‍ Monitor Message Quality WhatsApp uses customer feedback and engagement signals to assess business messaging quality. Meta also gives businesses information such as read rates to help them evaluate message frequency and relevance. Zoko's documentation notes that continued negative feedback can reduce delivery and may lead to templates being paused or disabled. Monitor quality before increasing campaign frequency. ‍ Understand WhatsApp Pricing in 2026 Meta switched WhatsApp Business Platform template messaging to per-message pricing on July 1, 2025 . Another important change arrives on October 1, 2026 . Meta has announced that service messages will become chargeable on a per-message basis. Meta's pricing documentation also lists upcoming changes affecting service and utility messaging during 2026. Businesses running high-volume marketing, support, or automated customer journeys should therefore review Meta's latest pricing when calculating campaign costs. ‍ How to Improve WhatsApp Blast Performance A strong campaign reaches the right customer with one clear reason to act. ‍ Segment Before Sending A smaller relevant audience can be more valuable than a large unrelated contact list. Segment using purchase history, product interest, customer lifecycle, location, or previous campaign behavior. ‍ Give Each Blast One Main Goal Choose one primary action: Shop a collection Reorder a product View a restock Claim an offer Reply for assistance Explore a launch Too many competing actions make the message harder to process. ‍ Use Customer Behavior Customer behavior gives campaigns context. A reorder reminder makes sense for an existing buyer. A launch announcement may work better for shoppers interested in that product category. ‍ Make Replies Easy WhatsApp is a conversational channel. Give customers an obvious way to ask questions about sizing, delivery, products, payment, or returns. ‍ Control Campaign Frequency Meta has introduced message limits, quality checks, customer feedback controls, and paid Business Broadcasts partly to reduce unwanted business messaging. Send when there is a useful message, not simply because another campaign slot appears on the calendar. ‍ WhatsApp Blast Metrics to Track Do not judge a broadcast only by how many messages were sent. WhatsApp Campaign Metrics Metric What It Tells You Delivery rate Whether messages reached recipients Read rate Whether recipients opened them Reply rate Whether the campaign started conversations Click-through rate Whether recipients followed the link or button Conversion rate Whether recipients completed the desired action Revenue Sales associated with the campaign Revenue per recipient Value generated across the targeted audience Opt-out rate Whether customers want fewer messages Negative feedback Whether targeting, content, or frequency needs attention For e-commerce businesses, conversion and revenue data provide more context than message engagement alone. ‍ How Zoko Helps Shopify Brands Send Targeted WhatsApp Blasts Shopify brands often outgrow manual broadcast lists as their customer database expands. Managing audience selection, personalization, campaign scheduling, exclusions, replies, and sales tracking across separate systems makes every broadcast harder to execute. Zoko connects Shopify with WhatsApp , giving merchants one platform for running targeted WhatsApp campaigns using their customer and store data. With Zoko, Shopify merchants can: Send Single Message or Series of Messages broadcasts Target broadcasts using customer tags and custom segments Use Shopify segments that automatically sync into Zoko Build segments from previous broadcast behavior Personalize templates with customer-specific variables Test broadcasts before sending them to the full audience Schedule campaigns for later delivery Review estimated maximum campaign cost before sending Enable conversion tracking for broadcast campaigns Automatically reattempt eligible failed messages Exclude customers who have opted out Route responses from specific broadcasts into custom team inboxes Zoko's current broadcast workflow includes testing, scheduling, estimated campaign cost, conversion tracking, and reattempt controls. Shopify-created customer segments can also sync automatically into Zoko and be used directly for broadcasts. Customers tagged OPT_OUT are automatically excluded from broadcasts by default, while custom inboxes can route responses from a specific broadcast to the appropriate sales or support agents. Zoko Broadcasts connect WhatsApp campaigns with Shopify customer data, audience behavior, conversations, and downstream sales activity. ‍ Common WhatsApp Blast Mistakes WhatsApp blasts usually become ineffective when volume becomes more important than relevance. Avoid: Buying WhatsApp contact lists Messaging customers without clear permission Sending every campaign to every customer Using unofficial bulk-sender tools Ignoring opt-outs Repeating promotions too frequently Sending irrelevant offers Adding several competing CTAs Launching without testing variables and links Failing to prepare for customer replies Tracking reads without measuring conversions Ignoring message quality and pricing changes The strongest WhatsApp blast is one the customer expected and has a reason to care about. ‍ Conclusion A WhatsApp blast can help businesses announce products, promote offers, re-engage customers, drive reorders, and start sales conversations. Effective campaigns depend on clear opt-in, relevant audience segmentation, suitable templates, controlled frequency, testing, and meaningful performance tracking. Zoko connects WhatsApp broadcasts with Shopify customer and purchase data, helping merchants segment audiences, personalize messages, manage campaign replies, and track conversions from one platform. Try Zoko for 7 days to start building WhatsApp campaigns around your Shopify customer journey. ‍ Frequently Asked Questions ‍ What Is a WhatsApp Blast? A WhatsApp blast means sending the same core message or campaign to many recipients. Businesses can use broadcast lists, Business Broadcasts, or WhatsApp Business Platform messaging depending on their needs. ‍ How Many People Can I Add to a WhatsApp Broadcast List? A standard WhatsApp broadcast list currently supports up to 256 contacts . Businesses needing larger and more advanced campaigns can consider Business Broadcasts or the WhatsApp Business Platform. ‍ Do Customers Need to Save My Number to Receive a WhatsApp Blast? For classic WhatsApp broadcast lists, yes. WhatsApp says contacts on the broadcast list need to have saved your number in their address book. Business Platform messaging uses a different permission model based on customer opt-in and approved business messaging. ‍ Can I Send a WhatsApp Blast to Thousands of Customers? Businesses can run messaging campaigns at larger scale through the WhatsApp Business Platform. They still need to follow Meta's opt-in, template, quality, messaging, and delivery requirements. ‍ Is WhatsApp Blasting Allowed? Yes. WhatsApp provides supported business broadcast and marketing-message features. Businesses must follow WhatsApp's opt-in and messaging policies, respect customer preferences, and comply with the privacy and marketing rules applicable to their markets. ‍ Can Businesses Send Promotional Messages Through WhatsApp? Yes. Promotional messages can be sent using marketing templates through the WhatsApp Business Platform to appropriately opted-in customers. Meta classifies messages intended to promote products, offers, or engagement as marketing messages. ‍ Is a WhatsApp Blast the Same as a WhatsApp Group? No. Broadcast recipients receive private messages, while members of a WhatsApp Group participate in the same shared conversation. ‍ Are WhatsApp Business Broadcasts Free? Meta has introduced Business Broadcasts inside the WhatsApp Business app as a paid feature . This is separate from classic broadcast lists and WhatsApp Business Platform pricing. ‍ How Can Shopify Stores Use WhatsApp Blasts? Shopify stores can use WhatsApp campaigns for product launches, restock alerts, personalized promotions, reorders, customer re-engagement, VIP campaigns, and other targeted customer communication. Platforms such as Zoko can connect these broadcasts with Shopify segments and customer data.

title: By the Numbers: How World Cup Fever Took Over Netflix
summary: Through series, docs, and games, and more, Netflix’s football slate captured a historic tournament and kicked off the countdown to the FIFA 2027 Women’s World Cup™.
body_text: Through series, docs, and games, and more, Netflix’s football slate captured a historic tournament and kicked off the countdown to the FIFA 2027 Women’s World Cup™. It’s been two weeks since the final whistle blew, but we’re still thinking about all the epic moments from the FIFA 2026 Men’s World Cup™. While it’s still another year until our broadcast of the 2027 Women’s World Cup in the US and Canada, fans couldn’t contain their excitement. Across series, films, documentaries, talk shows and games, our football slate lit up right alongside the tournament: Fandom By the Numbers The global football slate was stacked this year, with amazing selections from around the world, like Brazil ’70: The Third Star , México 86 , Colombia’s James , and Norway: The Dark Horse , as well as the official FIFA World Cup: Launch Edition video game, where you can star in your own World Cup story. In May alone, weekly views of Netflix's football titles more than doubled (over 250%) compared to weekly views in January through April. Views of Ronaldinho: The One and Only jumped 34% in Brazil in the hours after his halftime appearance. As Norway's run caught fire, Norway: The Dark Horse “rowed” its way to the #1 title in Norway in its first week on service. The series remained in Norway’s Top 10 throughout the entire tournament. The Rest Is Football: Checking in Like Friends Gary Lineker, Micah Richards and Alan Shearer delivered a daily fix of banter, analysis and hot takes throughout the tournament — becoming a ritual for fans checking in between matches. Episodes reached the weekly Top 10 in the UK, and the show’s already been renewed at Netflix for the 2026–27 Premier League season. Game On: Inside the Official FIFA Game This World Cup, we invited fans to star in their own match with the FIFA World Cup: Launch Edition game. Members could feel the thrill of the pitch instantly, playing for their country and stepping into real-life stadiums as the world’s best athletes. During the World Cup window, it was the #1 most-played Netflix game. Even after the final whistle of the championship, fans came back to the game in force — surging more than 40% above normal. And which teams were most popular in FIFA World Cup: Launch Edition ? Brazil took the lead, with Mexico and Argentina close behind. Players in Brazil were most likely to choose their home country, unlike in the US, where most players chose to play as Argentina: In the game, players can upgrade their favorite soccer stars using in-game currency that boosts attributes and unlocks new skill moves. From Vinícius Júnior in Brazil to Raúl Jiménez in Mexico, most gamers chose a hometown hero except for the US, where players spent most of their upgrades on Portugal’s Cristiano Ronaldo. And after teams won a real-life match, their fandoms flocked to the game, choosing to play as the winning team more than 2x as often as before. title: Pipeline Visibility: How Agencies Turn Data Into Forecasts
summary: Learn how pipeline visibility turns chaotic CRM data into reliable forecasts. Discover the metrics and roadmap agencies need.
body_text: 79% of sales teams miss quota because of poor pipeline management, and teams with strong pipeline visibility are 3× more likely to hit target. One revenue-operations guide also puts the average cost of a single misforecast deal at $14,000 per rep Executive Edge Magazine . That's why pipeline visibility isn't a reporting nicety. It's the difference between a forecast you can trust and a dashboard that keeps everyone busy while the quarter slips away. Why Most Pipeline Dashboards Are Lying to You A lot of teams think they have a visibility problem when they really have a trust problem. The dashboard looks full, the stages look busy, and the forecast call sounds confident, but the numbers still miss because the data behind them doesn't reflect what buyers are doing. The expensive gap is usually a data-quality problem hiding inside a reporting problem. Healthy pipeline coverage is usually 3 to 4 times quota , which means teams often need $3 to $4 in pipeline for every $1 of revenue goal just to absorb the slippage they know will happen Executive Edge Magazine . That benchmark is useful, but it can also lull leaders into a false sense of control. A team can carry enough volume and still lose if the stages are padded, the close dates drift, or the buyer is no longer engaged. Practical rule: if your forecast depends on rep optimism more than buyer evidence, your dashboard is giving you comfort, not clarity. For agency teams, the problem gets wider than sales. Pipeline visibility often breaks in the same place as time capture and utilization reporting, where leaders see activity on a screen but cannot trust the underlying inputs. That is why KPIs for internet marketing dashboards is a useful comparison point, because reporting only works when the measures are tied to real decisions. The better question is simple. What does the pipeline tell you about risk, momentum, and truth? If the answer is “not much,” then the issue isn't the chart design. It's the quality of the inputs and the discipline around them. Defining True Pipeline Visibility Pipeline visibility means having the real-time ability to see the status, health, and trajectory of every deal, who is involved, what has happened, and where the deal is headed. That is a narrower, more useful definition than “having dashboards.” A dashboard is a surface. Visibility is a decision system. For agency teams, the definition has to go further. True visibility also shows whether the work behind the pipeline is being captured accurately, because the same trust problem shows up in sales activity, time capture, and utilization reporting. Leaders can stare at a clean report and still be operating on stale inputs, late CRM updates, or timesheets that describe effort more neatly than reality. The definition only holds when the numbers reflect buyer motion and the actual use of team capacity. Visibility depends on data you can trust Visibility breaks when teams treat manual CRM updates as truth. If reps enter activity late, classify stages loosely, or rely on separate tools that do not sync, the CRM starts telling a story that looks complete but is not. A similar gap shows up in agency reporting, where leaders may have the right charts but not enough confidence in the underlying input. For a practical comparison point, KPIs for internet marketing dashboards shows how reporting only becomes useful when the measures are tied to real decisions. A stronger definition starts with clean stage rules, automated activity capture, and checks against real buyer behavior. More data does not solve the problem by itself. Better data does. The system has to separate seller activity from buyer motion and apply the same stage criteria every time, or the pipeline will look more stable than it is. The buyer has to matter more than the rep A rep can keep a deal “on track” in the CRM long after the buyer has gone quiet. Real visibility has to include observable buyer behavior, not just seller updates. If the buyer has not met, replied, reviewed, or brought in stakeholders, the stage label does not mean much. That same standard applies to agency work tracking. A project can look healthy in a timesheet report while the actual pattern of hours and capacity tells a different story. Marketing agency reporting only becomes useful when it shows what teams did, not what they hoped the record would say. Good visibility is about whether the system reflects reality, not whether it looks tidy. Key Pipeline Visibility Metrics The numbers that matter are the ones that show whether the pipeline is healthy, moving, and believable. Start with coverage, then test quality Pipeline coverage ratio is the first check. Healthy teams usually need a cushion above quota so they can absorb slippage and lost deals, but coverage by itself can still hide a weak pipeline if it is padded with opportunities that will never close. Pipeline velocity shows how quickly deals move through stages, which helps surface drag before it turns into missed revenue. Stage conversion rate shows where deals stop advancing, so you can see whether the problem sits in qualification, proposal, legal, or procurement. Deal aging shows how long an opportunity sits in each stage, which is usually where stalled deals start to show their real shape. A deal that sits too long in a stage is not just slow, it is asking for review. Use alerts, not guesswork Aging becomes useful when it triggers action. One operational guide recommends flagging deals that spend 1.5 times their average stage duration as a warning and 2 times as a red alert. That threshold matters because it turns a stagnant report into a decision. If a deal is still sitting in proposal or legal past that line, someone needs to ask a hard question about what is blocking it. Engagement signals round out the picture. Meeting frequency, multi-threaded contact, and competitive presence show whether the buyer is active or whether the deal is surviving on internal hope. That is the difference between a pipeline that looks full and one that can close. For agency leaders, the same logic shows up in marketing agency reporting . If a metric does not change a decision, it is just decoration. Common Pipeline Visibility Obstacles and How to Spot Them The biggest visibility problems usually hide in plain sight. Teams often think they need more reporting when what they really need is less noise and better discipline. Manual updates create delay Manual CRM entry is the oldest problem in the book. Reps get busy, notes go in late, and close dates drift until the pipeline starts reflecting memory instead of reality. By the time the data is updated, the quarter has already moved on. Fragmented tools hide the full story Conversation intelligence, buyer signals, and CRM records often live in separate places, which means nobody sees the whole deal in one view. That creates a false sense of completeness because each system tells part of the story, but none of them tells the whole one. If the rep's activity, the buyer's engagement, and the forecast category aren't connected, visibility is thin no matter how polished the dashboard looks. Loose stage definitions inflate the pipe When stage definitions are vague, reps classify deals in the most generous way possible. That inflates pipeline value without adding signal, and it makes the team feel healthier than it is. Weak stage discipline is one of the fastest ways to turn pipeline visibility into pipeline fiction. Coverage ratios can hide bad quality A team can have enough coverage and still miss target if the conversion rates are poor or the deals are aging badly. That's why coverage should never be the only thing leaders inspect. Quantity without quality just makes the forecast bigger, not better. A Tactical Roadmap to Improve Pipeline Visibility A dashboard does not fix pipeline visibility. A trustworthy process does. Define stage rules around buyer commitments Start with stage definitions a manager can enforce. Stages should be tied to observable buyer commitments , not vague optimism or a rep's best guess. Qwilr recommends flagging deals that sit too long without review Qwilr . That approach matters because it forces progression to rest on evidence, not on what someone hopes the deal will become. Clean the data sources before you add more tools A usable view starts with a CRM as the system of record, conversation intelligence for engagement signals, and a data enrichment layer for buyer context. Those inputs need to feed one synthesis layer so leaders can see the deal in one place instead of chasing it across tabs. If the system cannot separate real movement from logged activity, the forecast will keep drifting, and the dashboard will keep looking more certain than it is. For agencies, calendar-based time capture fills a gap that sales teams often miss. It connects actual effort to pipeline activity in a way the CRM usually cannot, which helps show whether the team's time is lining up with the deals in motion. That is a better read than activity counts alone because it ties work to the deal, not just to the log. If you are also thinking about agency-level lead generation , the same logic applies. More leads do not help if the system cannot tell you which ones are real, engaged, and worth the next hour of effort. Standardize tags and automate capture Once the stage rules are set, clean the properties that feed reporting. Use the same tags for client type, deal type, region, and workflow so the numbers mean the same thing across teams. Then automate activity capture wherever you can. Every manual field you remove lowers the chance of stale or sloppy data, and every clean field makes the forecast easier to trust. Put governance around aging and exceptions Weekly pipeline reviews work best when they focus on aging alerts, stalled deals, and stage-time limits. The point is not to put pressure on reps for its own sake. It is to force early review before a deal becomes an end-of-quarter surprise. The article on API data integration is useful if your team wants to move data cleanly instead of patching it by hand. Choosing the Right Tools and Integrations for Your Pipeline Tool choice should come after process choice, not before it. If you don't know how your stages work, what data matters, and which signals define a healthy deal, the tool just gives you another place to hide bad inputs. Compare tools by the job they have to do A basic CRM is the foundation, but it won't carry visibility on its own. You also need conversation intelligence to capture engagement, a synthesis layer to unify the signals, and dashboards that surface the metrics that matter. The best tool stack cuts manual work and improves confidence in the data. The wrong one adds another screen and another login. For agencies, the missing link is often the calendar. Calendar-based time capture connects actual effort to pipeline activity in a way a CRM can't, which matters when you're trying to understand whether the team's work pattern matches the deals in motion. That's a better lens than chasing activity counts alone because it ties the work to the deal, not just the log. If you're also thinking about agency-level lead generation , the same rule applies. More leads don't help if the system can't tell you which ones are real, engaged, and worth the next hour of effort. Look for integrations that reduce friction The best setup gives you rule-based tagging, flexible filtering, and exports for deeper analysis. It also plays well with the systems your team already uses, because visibility falls apart when people have to update one more field in one more place. If your stack still needs manual cleanup every week, it's not a visibility system. It's a reporting burden. Putting Pipeline Visibility Into Practice An agency can show a healthy pipeline on paper and still miss quarter after quarter if the team cannot see real buyer momentum. The fix starts with calendar-based time tracking that ties every client call, proposal session, and project review to the right deal, so leaders see actual effort instead of rough memory. Once that work is captured correctly, custom tags can sort it by project type, client tier, and revenue impact, which gives managers a clearer view of where time is going and why certain deals move while others stall. Rule-based alerts handle the gaps people miss. When a deal sits in proposal longer than the stage benchmark, the system can flag it before the weekly meeting, along with the last activity date, buyer engagement signals, and any competitive presence. That keeps managers from guessing and forces a review of the deals that have gone stale. It also cuts down on the polite team-room debate about whether the update is real or just cleanup in the CRM. I've seen this change forecasts because the team stops arguing about who updated what and starts looking at the same evidence. The rep still owns the deal, but the manager finally has a dependable view of the motion behind it. That's the point where visibility stops being a dashboard and starts acting like a control system, which matters if you want to learn how to improve forecast accuracy . If you want to tighten that loop, TimeTackle helps teams connect calendar activity, tags, and reporting so work shows up the way it happened. Calendar-based capture also gives agency leaders a cleaner read on utilization, which is the part most pipeline reports ignore until the quarter is already slipping.
